captions: Chapter two. The Retail King.
Our first verified winner made his fortune by doing
the opposite of everything the internet tells you.
He owns, essentially, one stock — and he almost
never talks about it.
Meet Radhakishan Damani.

By public filings, his disclosed equity is worth
around
one point nine eight lakh crore rupees — nearly
two trillion.
And here's the astonishing part: almost all of it
sits in a single company he founded and still
controls — Avenue Supermarts, the parent of DMart.
Sixty-seven percent of it.
The rest — VST Industries, a slice of three-M
India, a little United Breweries — barely moves the
needle.

Damani didn't spread himself across a hundred tips.
He
built one great business, and refused to sell it.
No interviews. No course. No channel. No calls.

Just decades of owning something excellent, and the
patience
to let it compound.
That patience is the entire strategy — and it's
the rarest thing on your feed.
Sit with that.
The richest retail investor in the country got there
slowly, in one business, in near-total silence.

The loudest voices online, meanwhile, are usually
selling access
to a secret they don't have.
Here's a rule of thumb worth keeping: the more

someone posts about their trades, the less you
should
trust their returns.
